questions.q: What happens when a user logs in from outside the org's Network Access trusted IP ranges?
options: Login is blocked entirely, with no fallback
Nothing — Network Access has no effect on login
The user must complete an identity-verification step (like a code), but isn't blocked outright
Their account is automatically frozen
questions.explain: Org-wide Network Access trusted ranges only add an identity-verification step for logins from outside the range.

questions.q: What happens when a user logs in from outside their profile's Login IP Ranges?
options: They're prompted for a verification code, same as Network Access
Login is blocked entirely — there's no verification-code fallback
Nothing changes; profile-level IP ranges are informational only
Their profile is automatically reassigned
questions.explain: Profile-level Login IP Ranges are a strict enforcement — logging in from outside the range is refused outright.

questions.q: Where do Login Hours and Login IP Ranges live in Setup?
options: Inside each individual profile
In Company Information
In the Translation Workbench
In the Object Manager
questions.explain: Both Login Hours and Login IP Ranges are profile-level settings, found on each profile's detail page.

questions.q: What does Login Access Policies control?
options: Which objects a profile can access
Whether admins can log in as other users without the user first granting access
The org's password complexity rules
Which permission sets are license-restricted
questions.explain: Login Access Policies is an org-wide security setting governing admin "log in as user" capability.

questions.q: If a user is logged in when their profile's Login Hours window ends, what happens?
options: They're immediately and forcibly logged out mid-action
Nothing happens until their next login attempt
They can still view their current page but can't take further action until their next allowed window
Their profile is automatically deactivated
questions.explain: A session already in progress when Login Hours ends isn't terminated, but no further actions are permitted until the next allowed window.
